462.note: Family-owned ice cream parlor on Federal Highway making 50-plus flavors on the premises daily, with walls full of license plates and antiques.
462.fn: Monroe Udell opened Jaxson's at its present Federal Highway location, just north of Stirling Road, in 1956; the family still owns it.

804.note: Oceanfront Deerfield Beach restaurant and tiki bar serving Bahamian conch fritters and fresh-caught fish.

1461.note: Oakland Park seafood restaurant open daily since 1984, with a separate stone crab menu in season.
1461.seas: Stone crab claws Oct 15 – May 1 (FWC season).
1461.fn: The restaurant says it has served South Florida seafood since 1984.

1625.note: Family-run steakhouse on Griffin Road since 1949, with an on-site butcher shop; the last of what was once a small chain of Tropical Acres restaurants.
1625.fn: Gene Harvey converted an old frame house on Griffin Road into the original Tropical Acres in 1949; it was gutted by fire on April 1, 1964 and reopened on the same site that November.

1770.note: Casual dock-and-dine raw bar near Port Everglades with free boat dockage, specializing in oysters and clams.
1770.fn: The raw bar's history says the current owners took over an existing beer-and-wine raw bar in the early 1970s and that it has served for over fifty years.

2164.note: Intracoastal waterfront restaurant and seafood market in Hollywood that cracks local stone crab claws in season and ships them from its market.
2164.seas: Stone crab claws Oct 15 – May 1 (FWC season).

2166.note: Hollywood Intracoastal restaurant with a patio dock, serving stone crabs in season, raw bar specialties and local fish.
2166.seas: Stone crab claws Oct 15 – May 1 (FWC season).

2822.note: Former Prohibition-era speakeasy and casino on an island off Lighthouse Point, reached by boat from Cap's dock, serving local fish and house-smoked fish dip.
2822.fn: Captain Theodore Knight moved his operation to the present site in 1928, building on a beached barge; it calls itself Broward County's oldest restaurant and is listed on the National Register of Historic Places (1990). The address is Cap's dock; the restaurant sits on an island reached by the restaurant's launch.
